facts.title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year
facts.summary: On Venus, one spin on its axis takes longer than a full trip around the Sun: about 243 Earth days to rotate once, compared with about 225 Earth days to complete an orbit.

facts.title: A Supermoon Can Look 14% Bigger and 30% Brighter Than the Faintest Full Moon
facts.summary: The Moon's orbit is not a perfect circle, so its distance from Earth keeps changing.

facts.title: A Teaspoon of Neutron Star Material Would Weigh Billions of Tonnes
facts.summary: A single teaspoon (4.9 millilitres) of neutron star material would have a mass of more than 5.5 × 10^12 kg, about 5.5 billion tonnes, or roughly 900 times the mass of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

facts.title: Alan Shepard Smuggled a Golf Club to the Moon and Hit Two Balls
facts.summary: On February 6, 1971, during the Apollo 14 mission, astronaut Alan Shepard became the first person to play golf on another world.

facts.title: Apollo Astronauts Brought 382 Kilograms of the Moon Back to Earth
facts.summary: Apollo astronauts collected 382 kilograms of lunar rock and soil from six places on the Moon's surface.

facts.title: Apollo Astronauts Said Moon Dust Smelled Like Spent Gunpowder
facts.summary: The Moon has a smell, but only astronauts have ever caught it.

facts.title: Aquarius Is the Tenth Largest of the 88 Constellations
facts.summary: Aquarius covers 980 square degrees of sky, making it the 10th largest of the 88 modern constellations.

facts.title: Astronauts Can Cry in Space, but Their Tears Don't Fall
facts.summary: Astronauts can cry in space, but their tears do not run down their cheeks.

facts.title: Georgi Ivanov Became Bulgaria's First Cosmonaut in 1979
facts.summary: On 10 April 1979, Georgi Ivanov became the first Bulgarian in space, launching from Baikonur aboard Soyuz 33 with Soviet cosmonaut Nikolai Rukavishnikov as part of the Intercosmos programme.

facts.title: China's Chang'e-4 Made the First Ever Landing on the Moon's Far Side
facts.summary: No spacecraft had ever landed on the far side of the Moon until January 3, 2019.

facts.title: During a Total Lunar Eclipse, the Moon Glows With Earth's Sunsets
facts.summary: In a total lunar eclipse the Moon slips completely into Earth's darkest shadow, yet it does not disappear.

facts.title: About 25 Tons of Space Dust Hit Earth's Atmosphere Every Day
facts.summary: Earth's atmosphere collects roughly 25 tons of cosmic dust every day, according to NASA.

facts.title: India Became the First Country to Land Near the Moon's South Pole
facts.summary: On August 23, 2023, India's Chandrayaan-3 mission set its Vikram lander down near the Moon's south pole, at roughly 70 degrees south latitude.

facts.title: Jupiter's Moon Io Is the Most Volcanically Active World in the Solar System
facts.summary: Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active world in the solar system, with hundreds of volcanoes.

facts.title: Katherine Johnson's Calculations Helped Send Americans Into Orbit and to the Moon
facts.summary: Katherine Johnson, an African American mathematician at NASA's Langley center, calculated trajectories for America's first human spaceflights and for the Apollo Moon missions.

facts.title: Lumpy Lunar Gravity Brought Down an Apollo 16 Satellite in Just 35 Days
facts.summary: The Moon's gravity is not smooth.

facts.title: NASA Crashed a Rocket Into the Moon in 2009 to Hunt for Water
facts.summary: In the early morning of October 9, 2009, NASA deliberately smashed a spent Centaur rocket stage into Cabeus crater near the Moon's south pole.

facts.title: Neptune Was First Spotted in Aquarius, Where Mathematics Said It Would Be
facts.summary: When Neptune was first identified on September 23, 1846, it lay in the constellation Aquarius, just north of Saturn in the sky.

facts.title: Nobody Saw the Moon's Far Side Until a Soviet Probe Photographed It in 1959
facts.summary: For all of human history, the far side of the Moon was hidden from view.

facts.title: Shadowed Craters at the Moon's South Pole Are Colder Than Pluto
facts.summary: Some of the coldest temperatures ever measured in the solar system were found on the Moon.

facts.title: Sound Cannot Travel Through the Near-Vacuum of Most of Space
facts.summary: Sound needs a medium such as air or water to travel through, and most of space is so close to a vacuum that sound waves have nothing to move through.

facts.title: Astronauts Say Space Leaves a Smell Like Hot Metal and Burnt Meat
facts.summary: Astronauts coming back inside after a spacewalk often notice a distinctive smell on their suits and tools: sharp and metallic, compared to hot metal, burnt meat or welding smoke.

facts.title: Sunlight Takes About 8 Minutes and 19 Seconds to Reach Earth
facts.summary: Light leaving the Sun takes about 499 seconds, slightly more than 8 minutes and 19 seconds, to cross the average distance to Earth.

facts.title: Thanks to a Gentle Wobble, We Can See About 59% of the Moon From Earth
facts.summary: The Moon always keeps the same face toward Earth because it rotates exactly once for every orbit; in a sense, its day and its year are the same length.

facts.title: Aquarius Has No First-Magnitude Stars Despite Its Large Size
facts.summary: Aquarius, the Water Bearer, contains no first-magnitude stars, even though it covers about 980 square degrees and ranks as the 10th largest constellation.

facts.title: The Average Color of the Universe Is a Pale Beige Called Cosmic Latte
facts.summary: If all the light in the universe were averaged together, it would look a pale, creamy beige, a shade astronomers named 'Cosmic Latte' (hex #FFF8E7).

facts.title: The Moon Drifts About 3.8 Centimeters Farther From Earth Every Year
facts.summary: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.

facts.title: The Moon Is Shrinking, and Apollo Seismometers Caught It Quaking
facts.summary: The Moon is still geologically restless.

facts.title: The Moon Was Probably Born When a Mars-Sized World Hit the Young Earth
facts.summary: Most scientists think the Moon formed from wreckage.

facts.title: The Moon's Largest Crater Is About 2,500 Kilometers Wide
facts.summary: The biggest scar on the Moon is the South Pole-Aitken basin, a giant impact crater roughly 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) across.

facts.title: The Pisces Constellation Is Home to the Circlet Asterism
facts.summary: The Circlet is a ring of seven stars in the western part of Pisces that marks the head of the constellation's western fish.

facts.title: The Sun Contains 99.86% of the Solar System's Mass
facts.summary: The Sun holds about 99.86% of all the mass in the Solar System, leaving just 0.14% for every planet, moon, asteroid and comet combined.

facts.title: Tree Seeds Orbited the Moon on Apollo 14 and Grew Into Moon Trees
facts.summary: Some trees growing in the United States have been to the Moon.

facts.title: Uranus Spins on Its Side, So Each Season Lasts About 21 Years
facts.summary: Uranus has an axial tilt of 97.77°, so it effectively rolls around the Sun on its side, and each of its four seasons lasts about 21 Earth years.

facts.title: Valentina Tereshkova Became the First Woman in Space in 1963
facts.summary: On 16 June 1963, Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and became the first woman in space.
